notes:
Account brief: mid-sized fintech (payments + fraud analytics) shifting heavy inference onto dedicated infra for latency-sensitive flows. Primary contact: CTO Priya Rao; Infra lead: Daniel Cortez. They run a mixture of chat-based support (low qps, high concurrency), real-time fraud scoring (strict p95 SLAs), and nightly reranking/embeddings pipelines. 

Key constraints / asks (from calls):
- p95 generation latency target: <= 125ms for short-chat responses (<=256 tokens) on dedicated capacity; p99 SLO discussion pending.
- Fraud scoring: hard requirement p95 <= 50ms end-to-end, sustained throughput 15k reqs/min at peak (bursty).
- Prefer VPC/private control plane; on-prem for sensitive PCI-adjacent workloads later.
- Want reserved GPU planning guidance: estimate initial commit 8 x A100-80GB equivalent; want warm pool strategy to reduce cold-starts.
- Autoscale: avoid linear overprovisioning; prefer fast scale-up (seconds) but gradual scale-down to avoid oscillation. Interested in predictive scaling using traffic windows.
- Warm pool retention: propose 10-15% of fleet kept warm, but they want cost vs benefit model.
- Queueing policy: prefer request queuing with backpressure and SLA-aware prioritization (checkout/fraud > chat).
- Fallbacks: multi-model routing (quantized cheaper variant) for non-critical reranking to save costs.

Quotes / call snippets: "If a checkout check takes >150ms we lose conversions — we need deterministic P95s." — CTO Priya Rao.
"We will not accept eviction of warm nodes during peak windows. Need explicit warm-pool guarantee in SLA." — Daniel Cortez (Infra).

- Jan 31: kickoff + requirements (fireflies ff-2026-01-31-epoch-eval).
- Feb 04: internal perf baseline run on hosted models (snapshot in Drive).
- Feb 12: infra deep-dive (ff-2026-02-12-infra-deepdive) — discussed scale policies, queueing thresholds, and pre-warm hooks.
- Feb 18: delivered draft Dedicated capacity proposal and cost model (drive link).

Technical notes captured from infra deep-dive:
- Desired scale-up speed: 20-40 seconds to add 2 GPUs under sustained queuing > 200 requests. Prefer ramp steps (2,4,8) not single large adds.
- Scale-down: cooling window >= 10 minutes after load drop; minimum warm-pool 1 GPU per availability zone.
- Warm pool behavior: cold-start time measured ~45s for full model load; warm instances reduce median latency by ~80ms. Cost impact: ~8% incremental committed spend for 15% warm pool.
- Queueing: implement priority queues; high-priority requests get preemptive allocation up to soft cap; excess high-priority requests spill to fallback model hosted_api.
- SLA points for negotiation: uptime 99.95%, end-to-end p95 guarantees per route, credits cap and measurement windows, notification for maintenance 72h, warm-pool eviction protection clause.
